open_obligations: Check whether verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria can be found with Chen et al.'s oracle-based algorithms.
Note the shift from regret minimisation to Stackelberg leadership.
Check whether the result needs the problem to have a valid proof system.
in.other_title: Theorem 8: valid interactive proofs = verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria of nip
in.rationale: Chen et al. ask for notions of equilibrium better suited to language games. Hammond and Adam-Day prove that a profile is a valid interactive proof system iff it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of nip, while noting worst-case losses and Stackelberg equilibria are hard to learn; Chen et al. instead use Nash equilibria of zero-sum games.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: which equilibrium notion suits learned oversight games, for prover-verifier messaging games

text: The authors propose games with very large action spaces as a formal model for language games and AI debate, calling it only a starting point. They pose further directions: different oracle models for best response, other notions of regret, and notions of equilibria better suited to these games.
title: Open: oracle models, regret notions and equilibria suited to language games
